<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:flatband}
If $U>0$, $N_{\mathrm b}\le D_{\mathrm{flat}}$ and $N_{\mathrm b}\le N$, the groundstate energy is
$E_0=N_{\mathrm b}\epsilon_{\min}+UN_{\mathrm b}/2$, and a groundstate lies in the color sector $(1^{N_{\mathrm b}})$, i.e., is totally antisymmetric in color.
 
For $N_{\mathrm b}=N$, it is an SU($N$) singlet.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Since $\tilde E_{k,k}\ge0$ and $\sum_k\tilde E_{k,k}=N_{\mathrm b}$,
$\langle H_{\mathrm{kin}}\rangle\geN_{\mathrm b}\epsilon_{\min}$.
 
Since $E_{i,i}$ has non-negative integer eigenvalues, $E_{i,i}^2\ge E_{i,i}$ and
$\langle\frac U2\sum_iE_{i,i}^2\rangle\ge UN_{\mathrm b}/2$.
 
Both bounds are saturated by the state whose orbital part is the antisymmetrized product of $N_{\mathrm b}$ linearly independent lowest-band orbitals, which exists since $N_{\mathrm b}\le D_{\rm flat}$: its orbital diagram $(1^{N_{\mathrm b}})$ forbids double occupancy.
 
For bosons, this orbital sector is admissible if and only if $N_{\mathrm b}\le\min(N,L)$, and the color diagram is then also $(1^{N_{\mathrm b}})$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
